data.title: Embers
data.intro: The Signal Tower has been dark for forty winters. Its beacon once answered ships, caravans and storms; now pigeons nest in the lantern room. The Guildmaster hands you a pair of brass headphones. “The tower doesn’t need eyes,” she says. “It needs ears. Every sound you learn lights a lamp on the stair. Light enough of them, and the beacon may remember how to speak.”

trial.name: The Gatekeeper
trial.text: The stair narrows at an iron gate. Behind it, a voice in the static sends without pause and never repeats. Copy 50 characters at 90% or better and the gate will open.

data.outro: The gate swings open onto the upper stair. For the first time in forty winters, a faint glow shows in the lantern room, and down in the square, people stop to look up.

data.text: The first lamp on the stair takes the flame. Somewhere below, old wiring hums awake.
A second lamp. The Guildmaster doesn’t look up from her ledger. “Two sounds. Everyone starts with two.”
Dust lifts from the steps as the third lamp wakes. On the landing lies the last operator’s logbook, its final entry unfinished.
The fourth lamp shows a brass key on the sill, warm, as if someone had only just set it down.
The shortest sound of all, and the brightest lamp yet. The pigeons leave the lantern room.
Six lamps. Out on the water, a fishing boat flashes its deck light at the tower. Coincidence, surely.
The seventh lamp lights a door marked RADIO ROOM. It is locked from the inside.
Eight lamps burn on the stair. The Guildmaster closes her ledger. “The Gatekeeper will want a word with you.”

data.title: The Upper Stair
data.intro: Above the gate the stair turns cold and narrow. The logbook speaks of “the far voice”: a station that kept calling the tower long after it went dark.

trial.name: The Warden of the Stair
trial.text: The Warden sends faster than the Gatekeeper and mixes every sound you know. Copy 50 characters at 90% or better.

data.outro: The second gate opens. The lantern room is close now, and somewhere in the static you are sure you heard someone call the tower by name.

data.text: The ninth lamp, and a draught from a broken pane. You stop the gap with a page from the logbook’s empty back.
The tenth lamp. The next page of the logbook is dated the night the beacon failed.
Lamp eleven shows a callsign scratched into the rail, half worn away by forty winters of hands.
Twelve lamps. Music drifts up from the Caravanserai; the city keeps later hours now that the tower glows.
The thirteenth lamp. In a hurried hand, the logbook says: “The far voice is getting weaker. I will answer tomorrow.”
The full stop lights the fourteenth lamp. Sentences can end now, and so can messages.
Lamp fifteen. The locked radio room hums whenever you pass its door.
Sixteen lamps. At the top of the stair waits a second gate, older than the first, with a speaking grille.
